claim: On neutral_hostile_v1/09_ml_artifacts, physical record cache misses dominate promoted G04 verification record() time; one zstd+delimiter record is the dominant individual owner.

decision.reason: Cache hits are effectively free: 96 hits consume about 0.09 ms total median, while 19 physical misses consume 203.13 ms and 83.40% of full policy verification. A single zstd+delimiter record consumes about 149.86 ms, roughly 73.8% of physical-miss wall time and 61.5% of total policy verification, despite its compressed payload being only 1,368 bytes. This strongly localizes the next optimization target to delimiter decode/inverse work rather than Zstd generally, record caching, node graph reconstruction, metadata opening, or the canonical verification wrapper.
decision.next_question: Can delimiter_inverse be expressed with exact block/strided slice reconstruction that preserves all bounds and bytes while replacing the current Python per-cell nested loop, and does that recover the measured runtime without changing archive bytes?

scope: One-workload instrumented research attribution only. The owner localization is strong on this exact substrate but is not itself product performance or release evidence.
